subject: Unresponsive egress - elevated 5xx/429 and retry storm
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@granitefin.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: support+aws@amazon.com, timothy.jensen@granitefin.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Elevated 5xx/429 across private deployment — started ~08:45 PT

Hi Stephanie / Rachel (cc: AWS),

We're seeing a pretty severe spike in errors and timeouts against the Redwood Private endpoints in our VPC starting ~08:45 PT. Symptoms: lots of 5xx from the inference endpoints, a growing number of 429s, and client retries stacking up (we're visualizing retry storms on our side). Latency has jumped from 120ms p95 to >2s p95 for some routes. This began right after we pushed a firewall rule change and a minor NAT config tweak to add an egress policy.

We've attached a short network flow dump and a pcap stub. Key indicators we see:
- Large number of TCP RSTs from the customer edge to Redwood IPs
- High SYN retry counts to the Redwood endpoints
- Client-side exponential retries are amplifying the error rate

Impact: production traffic for two finance workflows is degraded; customers are calling. We need immediate help to identify whether this is a Redwood routing/egress problem or something on our side. Can you triage urgently and advise mitigations (fallback, rate limiting, or rollback)?

Attachments: network-flows-20270528.txt, pcap-stub-20270528.zip, aws-support-ticket-12345.pdf

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Kim | SRE, GraniteFin
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@granitefin.com>, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, support+aws@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429 across private deployment — started ~08:45 PT

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and for sending the flow artifacts. I'm escalating this to engineering and ops. Initial ask: can you send the following ASAP so our investigation isn't blocked?

- NAT gateway metrics (port usage / port exhaustion) for the last 2 hours
- Firewall change diff (the rule that was pushed)
- Client retry configuration / backoff settings

Immediate mitigations we can try while we triage:
- If you have a hosted fallback route (hosted Redwood API) we can flip a config to route a subset of critical traffic to hosted for now.
- Implement short-term client-side throttling/backoff to break the retry amplification.
- We'll evaluate a temporary proxy at our edge to collapse retries and avoid upstream 429s.

I'm looping in Marcus (runtime) and Naomi (ops). Marcus — can you start by checking for 1) transient DNS failures on our egress, 2) any signs of upstream rate-limit triggers, and 3) whether our edge load balancer is returning 429s due to connection scarcity?

I'll keep Tim (CTO) and your execs updated as we have more.

- Stephanie
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.kim@granitefin.com, support+aws@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429 across private deployment — started ~08:45 PT

Stephanie / Naomi / Alex — quick findings from the runtime team after correlating our edge logs with the artifacts you shared. Summary: likely NAT port exhaustion combined with intermittent DNS failures + a tightened firewall ephemeral port rule. Evidence:

- Our ingress and service logs show many short-lived connections with TCP RSTs and client re-attempts; connection churn spikes at 08:46:00.
- The customer pcap shows outbound connections from many ephemeral ports that get reset; our logs show SYNs but low established socket counts — classic ephemeral port blocking.
- Our edge LB started returning 429s around the same time; those are downstream triggered because connection pooling collapsed and per-connection concurrency limits were hit.
- DNS: we see a rise in NXDOMAIN/timeout responses from the customer's forwarded DNS, which increases client-side retries and thus more new connections.

Immediate engineering actions we recommend (short-term):
1) Ask GraniteFin to revert the firewall change that restricts ephemeral ports (allow 1024-65535 outbound) — this is the highest-likelihood fix and should be low-risk.
2) If revert isn't possible quickly, we can provision a temporary proxy in Redwood Private to multiplex connections (collapse retries) for critical routes — 15-30m to spin up and validate.
3) Increase LB connection timeouts and bump concurrent connection limits temporarily.
4) Apply conservative 429 backoff (token-bucket based) at our edge to avoid cascading client retries causing sustained saturation.

Longer-term follow-ups:
- Add telemetry to detect NAT port exhaustion and fire a proactive alert to both parties.
- Recommend GraniteFin use NAT gateway scaling (or add additional EIPs) and reduce DNS TTLs or make DNS more resilient (forwarders).

I'm attaching a small extract of our connection table and the LB error histogram for the window — see network-flows-20270528.txt. Naomi — can ops coordinate the temporary proxy and the config changes if GraniteFin signs off?

- Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: alex.kim@granitefin.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, timothy.jensen@granitefin.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Action plan & maintenance window request — JIRA-OPS-9876

Alex / Team — thanks for the quick context. Per Marcus's analysis, ops is ready to proceed on the short path if GraniteFin agrees:

Planned actions (short-term, 45 minute maintenance):
- 12:30-13:15 PT: Apply firewall rule revert (restore ephemeral outbound range 1024-65535) on GraniteFin side (we will validate after change).
- 12:45-13:30 PT: Provision temporary Redwood proxy in GraniteFin Private deployment to collapse retries for critical inference routes (read-only rollout to start).
- 13:00-13:15 PT: Increase LB connection concurrency and bump ConnTimeout to 120s.

Rollback plan: if anything degrades, we will immediately pause the proxy and revert LB changes. We will not change customer data plane config beyond the proxy.

Risks: minimal if firewall revert is applied; highest risk is if the firewall change cannot be reverted or if additional undocumented rules exist.

Please confirm you approve the maintenance window. We have opened ticket JIRA-OPS-9876 and AWS support ticket 12345 is looped in (cc). We'll keep Tim and your execs updated every 30 minutes.

- Naomi
Sr. Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@granitefin.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: timothy.jensen@granitefin.com, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Action plan & maintenance window request — JIRA-OPS-9876

Naomi / Stephanie — we approved the maintenance window and rolled back the ephemeral port restriction at 12:32 PT. Observed behavior after change: immediate drop in TCP RSTs and the 5xx/429 curve started returning to baseline over ~20 minutes. The temporary proxy was helpful while traffic recovered.

Requests going forward:
- Please provide a post-incident writeup (we'll need it for our internal RCA and for our auditors).
- We will expect a credit for the production impact window (we lost SLA for ~45 minutes).

Thanks for turning quickly — Tim and the rest of execs are grateful for the responsiveness. We'll take the detailed artifacts and follow the JIRA ticket for the full postmortem.

Alex
Alex Kim | SRE, GraniteFin
